title: Independent complete literal source-image collation of the 1657 Cistercian Pater in both printed chant forms
reviewer: Independent AI literal source-image reviewer (1657 Cistercian complete Pater constituent)
scope: Complete bounded functional Pater constituent: raw0275 (printed213) RIGHT Orémus through the introduction, interleaved Extendit manus and dícere; all raw0276 (printed214) body text in both columns; raw0277 (printed215) LEFT through Sacerdos submissâ voce dicit, Amén. Both printed chant forms, the alternative-cantus governing rubric, its separately printed Per omnia/Amen, all responses and both final priest rubrics are included. The preceding Canon and raw0277 RIGHT Deinde/Libera are excluded.
method: Direct visual collation against the named source rasters and close crops, checked word by word across the complete bounded constituent. The candidate normalized bodies and their source-specific accents, spellings, punctuation, response cues and rubrics agree with the observed source under the declared normalization. Prior-review suggestions were independently tested against the images; no familiar prayer, OCR or other edition controlled a reading. Binding, extent, literal payload, all eight passage-selected unit bodies, facsimile witness and source JPEG/DjVu hashes were recomputed from actual bytes, rather than accepted from the neutral pin input.

findings_resolved.resolution: The close source crop supports dícere. with an acute on the first i only. No final e acute is read. The intervening red Extendit manus. remains between audémus and dícere in the stored source-block order.
The first Pater has dimítte; the second has dimitte without that acute. Both retain dimíttimus. The actual difference is preserved rather than harmonized.

The black pilcrow before Sequens is visible and retained as ¶. The printed iij. Lectionum and complete alternative-use rubric are retained, as are display initial cases PAter and PEr under the disclosed case-preserving normalization.

Both Sed líbera nos à malo. responses and the separately printed Per omnia response retain their actual crossed-R cue. The first closing rubric reads Sacerdos secretè dicit, with unaccented Amen.; the second reads Sacerdos submissâ voce dicit, followed by the qualified Amén. reading.

The final crop shows a dark raised hooked mark directly over the e of Amen where it meets a crease. I independently prefer the probable printed-acute reading Amén. The disclosed crease/wear reservation is necessary and adequate; this acceptance does not upgrade that diacritic to unqualified certainty.

The selected images contain both complete printed chant forms and their governing words. The final priest Amen closes the declared Pater selection on raw0277 left; the right-column Deinde/Libera belongs to the excluded wider continuation.

final_accent_qualification: Final Amén. is an accepted probable source reading: the dark mark above e is consistent with a printed acute but touches a crease in a worn area. This local uncertainty is explicitly retained in the binding and extent and does not conceal missing in-scope wording.
normalization_limit: NFC UTF-8; long s becomes s; unambiguous abbreviation signs expand only as individually documented; horizontal chant syllable spacing and physical line-end division hyphens join into words. Source u/v, i/j, ligatures, accents, case including display initials, punctuation, printed referrals, rubric wording and response markers remain. A printed pilcrow remains ¶ and response cue becomes ℟. Each stored LF is one consecutive source block distinguished by source wording, voice or ink; it is not newly inferred prayer paragraphing. Staff notation and pitches remain in the facsimile, not the Latin payload. No explanatory wrapper or source-completing wording is inserted.
review_limit: Complete only for this declared functional Pater constituent. All selected sung words are included; chant notes, staves and pitches are excluded from the Latin payload and remain in the facsimile. Whole-book, complete-Ordinary and wider post-Canon coverage remain partial. No acceptance of the concealed wider tail, reconstruction from another setting, historical ancestry, exact typeface geometry or contemporary liturgical authorization is supplied.
